sections.text:
Juha had a fat sheep that he raised to give him its wool and milk (if he had any).

Juha's friends were greedy for the lamb and wanted to eat it, so they came to him and said: "Oh Juha, have you heard the news? Tomorrow the Resurrection will take place and the world will end! What do you think we slaughter your lamb and give it a farewell feast and eat and enjoy before we die?"

Juha knew of their cunning, but he pretended to believe him and said: “As long as the resurrection is tomorrow, there is no problem. Take him and slaughter him.”

The friends went to the sheep and slaughtered it, took off their clothes, put them aside, and began swimming in the river until the meat was cooked.

Meanwhile, Juha collected all their clothes and set them on fire until they were completely burned!
When the friends came out of the river and did not find their clothes, they became angry and asked Juha: “Where are our clothes, Juha?! Who burned them?”

Joha answered coldly: “I burned it, and why are you angry? Didn’t you say that the Resurrection will be tomorrow? What will you do with the clothes after today?”

They knew that Juha had taught them a harsh lesson in response to their greed and cunning.
